Subject: Billing split + tax ownership for Pilot

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're getting our finance team lined up to accept the pilot terms, but there's a final technical question: when Redwood issues a single invoice for the pilot usage, we need a clear mapping that assigns VAT/tax liability and remit instruction per legal entity.

Current constraints on our side:
- We will remit to two of our legal entities depending on customer seat geography (US entity A & EU entity B).
- Tax treatment must be visible to our AP system (Vertex) via a consistent custom attribute on the invoice lines.

Can you share the proposed field mapping and a sample invoice (line-level) that shows how Redwood will expose entity_id, tax_owner, and remit_channel? TaxOps is looped for visibility.

Appreciate it — we need this to complete our procurement checklist next week.

Best,
Lena Morris
Head of Revenue Operations
Helium Health

Subject: Re: Billing split + tax ownership for Pilot

Lena — thanks for the clear ask. Quick reply from our side with an actionable artifact attached.

Summary / what we're proposing:
- Redwood will issue a single consolidated invoice file per billing period with line-level tags: entity_id, tax_owner_id, remit_account_id, and tax_rate_code.
- For each line we will include a custom 'vertex_tax_attr' string which your Vertex instance can consume (example values in attached spreadsheet).
- Payments can be routed to multiple bank accounts; the invoice will include 'remit_channel' per line and a summary section with payment instructions grouped by remit_account_id.

Action items for Helium Health:
1) Confirm which legal entity should be set as tax_owner for US vs EU seat pools.
2) Confirm Vertex ingestion team contact so we can validate schema.
3) Review the attached allocation_matrix_v1.xlsx and flag any mismatches.

I've CC'd Grace and Marissa from Finance/Ops to help finalize the matrix. If this works, we'll produce a sample test invoice in Vertex-friendly JSON.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

Thanks Ben — dug into the matrix and added a couple of clarifications (see comments column in allocation_matrix_v1.xlsx). Two operational notes:

1) Vertex attribute: we propose using 'vertex_tax_key' as a single concatenated field: {entity_id}|{tax_owner}|{tax_rate_code}. That keeps ingestion simple and avoids creating many optional columns. Example in vertex_config_snippet.txt.

2) Partial-line allocation: for some usage types (model-hosting vs prompt tokens) customers want a single line split across two entities. We can support fractional allocations (e.g., 70% entity A / 30% entity B) but need a confirmed rounding rule from Helium (round to cents on each line or aggregate at invoice summary).

Ask Helium: which rounding approach do you need? Also who on your Vertex team is the recipient for the test payloads?

Grace O'Connor
Head of Finance Operations, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.com
